bottom_line: In survivors of acute myocardial infarction with clinical evidence of heart failure, ramipril versus placebo reduced all-cause mortality with an observed risk reduction of 27% (95% CI 11% to 40%).
implications: Based on the reported intention-to-treat results, this document supports that in this selected post-AMI population with clinical evidence of heart failure, ramipril (vs placebo) was associated with lower all-cause mortality (170 deaths; 17% vs 222 deaths; 23%) and a reported 27% risk reduction (95% CI 11% to 40%). It does not establish effects for patients excluded from the trial (eg, severe heart failure/unstable angina/ACE-inhibitor contraindications) and does not by itself determine effects on specific non-mortality outcomes beyond the reported secondary composite and serious adverse event counts.

major_points.text: Multicentre, multinational, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study in 144 centres across 14 countries.
major_points.quote:
it was a
multicentre, multinational, double-blind, randomised, placebo-
controlled study. 2006 patients with acute myocardial infarction
 and clinical evidence of heart failure were recruited in 144 centres
 in 14 countries.

major_points.text: Patients were randomised to placebo or ramipril, with treatment started in hospital between day 3 and day 10 after AMI.
major_points.quote:
randomly allocated to double-blind treatment with either
 placebo (992 patients) or ramipril (1014 patients) on day 3 to
 day 10 after AMI (day 1).

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was all-cause mortality analysed by intention-to-treat.
major_points.quote:
The prespecified primary
 statistical endpoint was all-case ("intention-to-treat"),
 all-cause mortality.

major_points.text: Serious adverse events were reported less frequently with ramipril than placebo, but hypotension was more common with ramipril.
major_points.quote:
There were fewer patients with reported serious adverse
events on ramipril, 581 (58%), than placebo, 625 (64%).

absolute_effects.text: All-cause mortality: 170 deaths (17%) with ramipril vs 222 deaths (23%) with placebo.
absolute_effects.quote:
There were 170 deaths
(17%) in the ramipril group and 222 (23%) in the placebo
group

absolute_effects.text: Serious adverse events: 581 (58%) on ramipril vs 625 (64%) on placebo.
absolute_effects.quote:
serious adverse
events on ramipril, 581 (58%), than placebo, 625 (64%).

absolute_effects.text: Syncope: 24 (2-4%) on ramipril vs 17 (1-7%) on placebo.
absolute_effects.quote:
Syncope was reported for 24 (2-4%) patients
on ramipril and 17 (1-7%) on placebo

absolute_effects.text: Hypotension: 42 (4-2%) with ramipril vs 23 (2-3%) with placebo.
absolute_effects.quote:
hypotension in the ramipril treated
group-42 (4-2%) compared with placebo 23 (2-3%).

subgroups.text: Subgroup effects were examined using interaction terms in Cox proportional hazards regression model.
subgroups.quote:
Subgroup effects were examined by including interaction terms in
the Cox proportional hazards regression model.

subgroups.text: All estimated relative hazards were below 1 and no interaction test was significant at the 5% level.
subgroups.quote:
All the
estimated relative hazards were below 1 and in no case was
the test for interaction significant at the 5% level.

harms.text: Serious adverse events were reported in 58% on ramipril vs 64% on placebo.
harms.quote:
There were fewer patients with reported serious adverse
events on ramipril, 581 (58%), than placebo, 625 (64%).

harms.text: Hypotension occurred more often with ramipril (4-2%) than placebo (2-3%).
harms.quote:
hypotension in the ramipril treated
group-42 (4-2%) compared with placebo 23 (2-3%).

harms.text: Syncope was reported in 2-4% on ramipril vs 1-7% on placebo.
harms.quote:
Syncope was reported for 24 (2-4%) patients
on ramipril and 17 (1-7%) on placebo

harms.text: Renal failure occurred with similar frequency: 15 (15%) on drug vs 12 (1-2%) on placebo.
harms.quote:
Renal
failure occurred with a similar frequency in the two groups:
15 (15%) on the drug and 12 (1-2%) on placebo.

harms.text: Premature withdrawals from study drug: 352 in ramipril group vs 318 in placebo group.
harms.quote:
In total there were 352
premature withdrawals from the ramipril group and 318
from the placebo group.

harms.text: Intolerance contributed to 126 ramipril withdrawals vs 68 placebo withdrawals.
harms.quote:
Intolerance was given as the
primary or a contributory factor in 126 of the ramipril
withdrawals and in 68 of the placebo withdrawals

guidelines_referenced.text: European Guidelines for Good Clinical Research Practice
guidelines_referenced.quote:
study
conduct adhered closely to the European Guidelines for Good
Clinical Research Practice.

inclusion_criteria.text: Aged at least 18 years with definite AMI and clinical evidence of heart failure at any time after the index AMI.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
All patients aged at least 18 years admitted to coronary care,
 intensive care, or general medical units with a definite AMI and
 clinical evidence of heart failure at any time after the index AMI

exclusion_criteria.text: Severe heart failure (usually NYHA grade IV).
exclusion_criteria.quote:
Patients with severe heart failure (usually NYHA
grade IV)

exclusion_criteria.text: Heart failure of primary valvular or congenital aetiology.
exclusion_criteria.quote: heart failure of primary valvular or congenital aetiology

exclusion_criteria.text: Recognised contraindications to ACE inhibitor treatment.
exclusion_criteria.quote:
any of the recognised contraindications to
ACE inhibitor treatment were excluded from the study.

analysis_methods.quote:
The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, analysed by
intention-to-treat.

analysis_methods.text: Kaplan-Meier survival curves and log rank test used for comparison.
analysis_methods.quote:
Survival curves were obtained by use of the
Kaplan-Meier estimate, and the log rank test was used for
comparison of the two groups (ramipril and placebo).

analysis_methods.text: Cox proportional hazards regression model used to obtain relative hazard and 95% CI.
analysis_methods.quote:
The relative
hazard and corresponding 95% confidence interval (CI) was
obtained by fitting a Cox proportional hazards regression model
with a single covariate-namely, the allocated treatment.

analysis_methods.text: Interim analysis plan and rationale for no adjustment to final analysis.
analysis_methods.quote:
so that no adjustment was required
to the final analysis to compensate for this interim analysis.

analysis_methods.text: Estimated about 2000 patients based on predicted placebo mortality and a clinically relevant improvement defined as 25% reduction in all-cause mortality.
analysis_methods.quote:
On the following assumptions the trial was estimated to require
about 2000 patients: predicted average patient follow-up 15
months; predicted placebo mortality 20% at 15 months; a
"clinically relevant improvement" defined as a 25% reduction in
all-cause mortality

trial_conduct.text: An independent adjudicating panel acted as the overall ethical supervisory body and had access to the randomisation code.
trial_conduct.quote:
An independent adjudicating panel (IAP) acted as the overall
ethical supervisory body and had access to the randomisation code.

trial_conduct.text: All endpoints were validated by a subcommittee of the international steering committee.
trial_conduct.quote:
All endpoints were validated
by a subcommittee of the international steering committee.

trial_conduct.text: Independent group conducted prospective audits to ensure adherence to European Guidelines for Good Clinical Research Practice.
trial_conduct.quote:
An
independent group was responsible for conducting a series of
prospective audits of study procedures, to ensure that the study
conduct adhered closely to the European Guidelines for Good
Clinical Research Practice.

trial_conduct.text: Planned interim analysis after 175 deaths with stringent stopping rule p < 0-001 for early termination.
trial_conduct.quote:
A planned interim analysis was performed after 175 deaths, half
way through the projected total of 350 deaths. A very stringent
stopping rule was specified in the protocol (p < 0-001 was the
guideline for early termination)

criticisms.text: Hospital admission data were not part of the prespecified primary or secondary analyses, and were not shown.
criticisms.quote:
there were fewer
 admissions to hospital (data not shown), as would be
 expected from the mode of action of ramipril and the
 findings of other trials; but hospital admission was not
 specified as part of the primary or secondary analyses.

criticisms.text: A substantial proportion were no longer taking randomised medication by 18 months, and many withdrawn from placebo were taking open-label ACE inhibitor.
criticisms.quote:
by 18 months 40% of patients (excluding those
who had already died) were no longer taking randomised
medication and that most of the patients withdrawn from
placebo were taking open-label ACE inhibitor.

criticisms.text: One centre was excluded because its data were inconsistent.
criticisms.quote:
During the course of the study it became apparent that data from
one centre were inconsistent.
